summary: @servicetitan/cp-mfe-dev preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated math_init.js
details: package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is itself obfuscator.io-shaped (variable names like `_0x488df8`, per-function property-dispatch objects) and, at install time, downloads a pinned Bun v1.3.13 platform-specific archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts it to a temp directory, marks the Bun binary executable, and invokes it against `math_init.js` shipped in the tarball root. math_init.js is a 727,680-byte single-line file with the classic obfuscator.io shape (large numeric/string lookup array `n7gIxM`, string-array rotator `WV8StW`, custom base decoder `hc1jfK9`); its runtime network destinations are hidden behind that decoder and cannot be resolved statically. math_init.js is not listed in package.json `files` (`["dist","local","src"]`) — an undeclared tarball blob smuggled past the declared file manifest. The payload is executed under a downloaded alternate runtime (Bun), bypassing Node-based install-time inspection. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: an npm library package has no legitimate reason to pull a second language runtime at preinstall to run an opaque obfuscated blob under the installer's user privileges.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
